model_output.verdict: A senior outpatient physical therapist whose patient load, programs, mentoring, and patient-reported results are easy to see.
write_up: A recruiter sees a licensed Minnesota physical therapist with outpatient orthopedic and sports rehab experience, plus mentoring and scheduling work. Your resume isn't going to be the reason you don't hear back. How competitive a particular job is will also matter.

The return-to-run program line is a great model: you built a named program and say how many patients completed it. One useful addition would be the measure and patient count behind the 2025 function scores.

cards.line: - Built a return-to-run program that 85 patients completed in 2025
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this line. It gives a recruiter both your role in the program and a concrete picture of its use.

cards.line: - In 2025, 92% of discharged patients improved their patient-reported function scores
cards.cannot_tell: This is a strong result, but a recruiter can't tell how many discharged patients are included or which measure was used. Those details would give the percentage more context.
cards.example: In 2025, 92% of [number] discharged patients improved their patient-reported function scores on [measure]
cards.question: How many discharged patients were included, and which function measure did they complete?

fit.note: Your experience points toward outpatient orthopedic physical therapy, including sports and post-surgical rehab. The mentoring and aide scheduling add senior-level responsibilities.
